html:
José Santos Zelaya was the liberal president of Nicaragua from 1893 to 1909. He modernised the state, annexed the Caribbean coast, and was overthrown with American backing.

He separated Church and state, built schools, railways and ports, and encouraged coffee planting. In 1894 he sent troops to annex the Miskito Reserve, uniting the country's two coasts for the first time. He also ruled harshly, and dreamt of uniting Central America under his leadership.

He fell out with the United States when he sought other partners for a canal across Nicaragua, after Washington chose Panama. In 1909 he had two Americans executed for aiding rebels. Washington backed the rising, he resigned, and soon US Marines landed, starting the long occupation. He belonged to the age of liberal strongmen like Porfirio Díaz.
